subtitle: Precision, memory, communication and noise costs of reproducing CHSH statistics, stated from typed, test-backed claims
author: Jaden Fix

claims.name: canonical CHSH metric
assumptions: canonical CHSH schedule with equal setting weights
declared two-parameter coplanar visibility-phase CHSH family
nonclaims: concerns one-trial predictive total variation only

claims.name: Delft 2015 on the disk
claims.status: finite check; reproduces the published statistic
assumptions: standard-library port of the published valid-trial filter applied to the released Delft 2015 data (n = 245)
published bound on the setting-generator bias
nonclaims: a Bell violation is not evidence for simulation
the fixed-n p-value assumes n fixed in advance

claims.name: dithering boundary
assumptions: laws on four outcomes
the renderer may draw fresh private randomness on every trial
nonclaims: not new
finite precision is untestable only when private dithering is unrestricted

claims.name: commensurable schedules cannot identify
assumptions: every setting cosine is a rational multiple of one number
4 divides D
the visibility range is wide enough: c (v_max - v_min) >= 4b / D
stationary renderer
nonclaims: no claim for odd D or for D below the threshold

claims.name: canonical CHSH (commensurable case)
assumptions: canonical CHSH settings, all |c_j| = 1/sqrt(2)
4 divides D and D (v_max - v_min) >= 4 sqrt(2)
unknown visibility
nonclaims: the 5-bit (D = 32) renderer is an example, not a claim about the Delft source

claims.name: the threshold is needed
claims.status: finite check; boundary witness recorded in the ST-T287 record
assumptions: CHSH with v in [9/10, 1] and D divisible by 4 in [4, 400]; and v in [1/2, 1]
nonclaims: a bounded counterexample to the unconditional statement, not a general classification

claims.name: settings 0 and pi/4
assumptions: schedule contains a setting with cosine 1 and one with cosine 1/sqrt(2)
v_min > 0
attainment and trial counts restricted to designs with cosines in {0, +-1, +-1/sqrt(2)}, 4 divides D, D >= 4 / (v_max - v_min)
nonclaims: exactly known cosines; IEEE-754 floating point and angle discretization are out of scope

claims.name: universal converse and known unit visibility
assumptions: (a) fixed horizon or almost surely bounded stopping time, K-outcome trials, D > K / 4
(b) visibility known to be exactly v = 1, angle set exactly to cos theta = 1 - 2/D, D even
(c) fixed angle pi/4, v = 1 known, D = 2^k with k >= 3
nonclaims: with v_max < 1 the rare-outcome mechanism of (b) disappears and no Theta(D log(1/eps)) rate is claimed

claims.name: digits and constants
assumptions: k = 3..64 with exact integer-square-root decisions and 80-digit arithmetic
declared grid of 110 values of D <= 10^4 and v in [1/2, 1]
nonclaims: grid values corroborate, but do not replace, the proved constant 1/(3 + 2 sqrt(2))

claims.name: area converse
assumptions: rank-2 schedule
epsilon-accurate one-trial renderer with arbitrary emissions
declared two-parameter coplanar visibility-phase CHSH family
nonclaims: one-trial bound; n-trial, adaptive or transcript-level renderers are not covered

claims.name: canonical CHSH memory
claims.status: upper bounds new; lower bound new as applied (also from the ST-T05 packing)
assumptions: canonical CHSH schedule
epsilon <= 1/8 for the in-family count
nonclaims: clipped emissions need not be quantum-realizable
internal states are representational resources of a hypothetical renderer, not claims about parent hardware

claims.name: universal ceiling
assumptions: finite schedules
nonclaims: not new

claims.name: tiling schedules are exact
assumptions: exactly two or three direction classes
nonclaims: no exact constant for four or more classes

claims.name: most memory with at most three classes
assumptions: rank-2 schedules with at most three direction classes
nonclaims: the hexagon is not the maximizer over all finite schedules (ST-T295)

claims.name: the hexagon does not force the most memory
claims.status: lower end new as applied; upper end classical and cited (Rogers asymptotic covering theorem; Fejes Toth lattice covering bound for centrally symmetric convex discs); new: A_4 < 18 sqrt(3)
assumptions: rank-2 schedules
rational enclosures certify A_4
nonclaims: the supremum over finite schedules is only bracketed, not computed
the lattice covering bound is Fejes Toth's and is cited, not reproved

claims.name: local and global rankings differ
assumptions: center Fisher information of the declared family
nonclaims: local Fisher optimality is not claimed to rank schedules for memory

claims.name: one-way signaling
claims.status: (b) is Pironio's bound; (a) no earlier statement found but may be known; (c) is a trivial finite analogue of Toner and Bacon
assumptions: uniform settings independent of the shared randomness and of the past
per-trial communication budget
nonclaims: (b) is not new
one bit is the worst-case cost only
budgets that hold only on average need an Azuma-type argument that is not given

claims.name: measurement dependence
assumptions: local outputs
input law may depend on the hidden variable with p(s, t | omega) >= l
CHSH bound S <= 4 - 8l under uniform observed inputs
nonclaims: not new

claims.name: detection efficiency
assumptions: Tsirelson behavior with independent symmetric detection efficiency eta and a no-click outcome
nonclaims: not new; not tested on Delft (event-ready)

claims.name: statistical strength
claims.status: value at v = 1 is that of van Dam, Gill and Grunwald; the visibility family and data-processing proof are new
assumptions: uniform inputs
local laws with uniform inputs
nonclaims: the v = 1 value is not new

claims.name: anytime-valid tests and their limits
assumptions: null holds conditionally on the past
data-independent mixtures or predictable bets
for the Wald floor, an almost surely finite stopping time with finite mean
nonclaims: not new

claims.name: exact one-trial deficiency
claims.status: closed form new; framework and reduction standard (Le Cam; Torgersen)
assumptions: one-trial interface
equal correlation magnitudes C (unequal magnitudes only under worst-setting aggregation)
central post-processing
0 <= lambda < 1 for the strict inequalities
nonclaims: Bell-local and n-trial deficiencies are not computed

claims.name: risk transfer
claims.status: standard (easy direction of Le Cam's randomization criterion)
assumptions: bounded loss
nonclaims: not new

claims.name: deterministic disguises are worse
claims.status: new; step (a) is a computer-assisted exact proof
assumptions: deterministic setting-preserving kernels (a relabeling chosen per setting)
0 < C < 1 and 0 <= lambda < 1 for (d)
nonclaims: compares only deterministic setting-preserving relabelings with the optimal central kernel of ST-T306

claims.name: canonical CHSH deficiency audit
assumptions: lambda on the grid {0, 1/8, ..., 1}
canonical CHSH and one declared rational schedule
nonclaims: bounded corroboration, not a proof

claims.name: Delft 2015, constant-bet mixtures, negative
assumptions: constant-bet mixtures on the CHSH win indicator fixed independently of the data
per-trial budgets
the published setting-predictability model
nonclaims: concerns constant-bet mixtures on the win indicator only
nothing in this section adjusts for the fixed-n chi-square p = 0.046 against uniform setting frequencies

context_note: cited in prose or tables as context; stated in the repository, not restated as a result environment here
paper_nonclaims: nothing in the paper is evidence for or against simulation
internal states and grid denominators are representational resources of a hypothetical renderer
typed and test-backed means executable tests and exact receipts, not formal proofs
prior-art searches were not exhaustive; 'new' means no earlier statement was found
